title: Cosmic Insignificance Therapy
coreMove: Cosmic insignificance therapy does not deny meaning; it lowers the standard from permanent fame to finite care, useful work, and attention to nearby lives.

exampleSpecs.audience: a product manager measuring normal work against heroic legacy language
exampleSpecs.stakes: a useful release may be dismissed as failure because it is not historic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Steve Jobs, the iPhone, Silicon Valley, and dent-in-the-universe language to shrink an inflated standard.

exampleSpecs.audience: a graduate student comparing an ordinary life with genius biographies
exampleSpecs.stakes: an impossible standard could turn honest work into self-contempt
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Iddo Landau's standard-setting argument with Michelangelo, Mozart, and Einstein.

exampleSpecs.audience: a novelist tempted to quit because her audience is small
exampleSpecs.stakes: creative labor may stop if public acclaim becomes the only valid proof
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Leo Tolstoy, War and Peace, novelist, and public acclaim to test finite-audience meaning.

exampleSpecs.audience: a tenant disappointed that a crisis did not remake society
exampleSpecs.stakes: local care may be dismissed because it is not sweeping transformation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the coronavirus pandemic, Great Pause, neighbors, and 2020 to value modest social change.

exampleSpecs.audience: a parent whose caregiving feels too ordinary to count
exampleSpecs.stakes: daily care may be devalued when compared with celebrated genius
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Iddo Landau and Einstein to expose the wrong standard for ordinary care.

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer deciding how to describe modest community work
exampleSpecs.stakes: honest service may be inflated into a grand story or discarded as too small
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Great Pause, coronavirus pandemic, neighbors, and 2020 to show a decision already made.
